subject.title: feat(gateway): wire coding tools into /tools/invoke HTTP surface

question: After deciding the read-only proposal, should owner-authenticated Gateway direct invocation also expose built-in host filesystem `write` and `edit` behind the class opt-in, per-tool allowlist, and owner gate?
rationale: Code review supports the enforcement design, but remotely callable built-in host mutation changes the intended Gateway trust boundary and requires explicit Gateway/security owner intent.

options.title: Land read first
options.body: Review and land the separate read-only PR, then restack this PR as a write/edit-only proposal for a distinct security decision.

options.title: Approve the full stack
options.body: Accept read, write, and edit together after resolving the branch conflict and repeating exact-head live proof.

options.title: Keep filesystem tools agent-only
options.body: Reject built-in filesystem direct invocation and retain agent-mediated or plugin-owned alternatives.

recommendation.title: Land read first
recommendation.body: Review and land the separate read-only PR, then restack this PR as a write/edit-only proposal for a distinct security decision.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged history most directly owns HTTP tool-invoke authorization, owner identity, and trusted-proxy guardrails involved in this decision.
